about: A Zork II style underground cavern: a barrow, a cavern with a ravine, a formal garden with a unicorn, a disorienting Carousel Room, a riddle door, and a well with a bucket. A Wizard pops in at random and casts small spells on you. I spent most of my time trying to get the bucket to carry me up the well.

done.why: I poured water into the bucket while standing outside it. It rose and never came back. I waited, explored and tried a few things, but the way up stayed closed. I had also seen most of the reachable rooms.

moments.note: The Wizard appeared and cast Fear, which sent me into the Carousel Room.
I poured water into the bucket without sitting in it. It went up and never came back.
The Carousel Room scrambled my directions, and the Wizard's spells made later moves unreliable too.
The rope and wall gave no way forward.

wished: A hint about how the bucket comes back down
A way to carry more water at once
A map of the Carousel Room exits

lines.line: There is a deafening clap of thunder and the stone door quietly swings open to reveal a passageway beyond.
lines.why: Answering the riddle with 'well' worked, which was a nice payoff.

lines.line: It is a wooden bucket, 3 feet across and 3 feet high, bound with iron hoops...
lines.why: Rich description that set up the puzzle.

fun.why: I liked the Zork nostalgia and the random Wizard. The stuck bucket puzzle was a drag.

engagement.why: I stayed curious about the places I could reach, but I stalled when the bucket did not return.

difficulty.why: The bucket never came back down, and I could not tell what to do about it.

interestingness.why: The world has lots of rooms, a roaming Wizard, and spells that change what you see and where you go.

prose.why: The descriptions are evocative and detailed.
